answer: An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the garden ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Because the age is read from the raven checkpoint rather than self-declared, the harbor audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. Running a farm as a result means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. That is 34 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
